newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shun Tak consortium seeks HK$6.4 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Shun Tak consortium seeks HK$6.4 bln loan.

text.p: Shun Tak Holdings Ltd confirmed on Wednesday a Shun Tak-led consortium was seeking a loan of about HK$6.4 billion to fund its Belcher Gardens property development project in Hong Kong.
Director Daisy Ho told reporters she hoped the financing arrangement will be finalised by the end of this month.
Ho said she expected the new loan to be the final facility for the financing of the residential redevelopment, which is estimated to cost about HK$11 billion.
The project is held 50 percent by Shun Tak, 29 percent by Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, and 10 percent by each of New World Development Co Ltd and Liu Chong Hing Investment Ltd.

Pansy Ho, another director at Shun Tak, said she expected the interest rate for the loan to be reasonable by market standards although it was expected to be higher than that of Shun Tak's HK$1.8 billion revolving credit facility signed on Wednesday.
Banks participating in that facility received an all-in return of between 103 to 108 basis points, said an executive at BNP Hong Kong, arranger of the latest loan.

About half of the HK$1.8 billion loan, the largest Shun Tak has ever accessed, will be used to finance the redevelopment of Belcher Gardens, said Daisy Ho. The rest will be used as general working capital.
Daisy Ho said the company's gearing ratio would be about 0.7 to 0.8 if the loan was fully drawn.
Pansy Ho said Shun Tak was happy with the Belcher Gardens redevelopment premium of HK$4.9 billion.
Shun Tak chairman Stanley Ho said construction of the project would start towards the end of next year and pre-sale of uncompleted units would also begin in late 1997.
He expected the residential units to be sold for about HK$5,500 to HK$6,000 per square foot.
